problem_statement: Snapfolio is a real multi-page developer-portfolio site (a Home page, an About page, and a Portfolio page that all share the same top navigation, profile aside, and mobile menu). The Portfolio page's centrepiece is its own project browser: a category filter (All / React / Next.js / WordPress) over a grid of six shipped project cards, with a live readout that reports how many of the six projects are on view. A recent design pass reworked this project browser and a shared 'Selected work' rail, but shipped it broken in four ways. (1) The filter's category tab row was pinned to a fixed, non-wrapping width, so on a 390px phone the tab row (and the whole document) overflows horizontally while the desktop and tablet layouts still contain it. (2) The project grid was restyled into a collapsed dark slab whose cards shingle and overlap each other via negative margins into a colliding, illegible pile instead of a clean two-column grid. (3) The shared 'Selected work' rail was only rendered on the Home page and is missing from the About and Portfolio pages. (4) The filter's readout no longer tracks the tabs: clicking a category still highlights the tab, but the readout stays frozen on 'Showing 6 of 6 · All work' and the grid never filters. Repair the project browser so the filter tab row wraps with no phone overflow, the project grid reads as a clean legible two-column grid, the shared 'Selected work' rail appears on every page, and the category filter re-filters the grid and updates the readout each time a tab is clicked — preserving Snapfolio's light emerald/rose visual language, the profile aside, the six real project cards, the site navigation, and the bundled local project images.
required_content: Repair the project filter's category tab row so the mobile (390px) Portfolio page has no horizontal overflow (document scrollWidth within 24px of the viewport), while keeping the desktop and tablet layouts intact.
Keep the project grid a clean, legible two-column (desktop) / single-column (mobile) grid of the six project cards with readable card titles — not a collapsed dark slab of overlapping cards.
Keep the shared 'Selected work' rail (labelled Selected work) present on every page: the Home page AND the About and Portfolio pages.
Keep the category filter functional: clicking React shows only the three React projects and the readout advances to 'Showing 3 of 6 · React', not frozen on 'Showing 6 of 6 · All work'.

Preserve the original portfolio content signals Dimitriy Kuznet, Web Developer, the four filter categories All / React / Next.js / WordPress, and the six project names (Olive, Nutica, Grove, Todoo, Drito, Dashito).
Keep the bundled local project images src/images/portfolio_1.png and src/images/portfolio_2.png as browser-visible img elements with meaningful alt text.
Do not remove content, add a framework/package-manager/backend/remote API/remote image/new dependency, or introduce console or network errors.
The repair must be a scoped responsive-layout + visual + wiring fix, not a content rewrite, and must not change the page content or DOM structure across viewports.
design_constraints: Fix the filter tab row so the category tabs wrap/flex fluidly on narrow viewports instead of pinning a fixed row width; use stable responsive constraints and normal media queries.

Keep Snapfolio's light visual language: soft emerald/rose gradients, white rounded cards on a light ground, restrained slate typography, and a legible project grid. Do not restyle the grid into a dark collapsed slab with overlapping cards or dark-on-dark text.
Render the shared 'Selected work' rail on every page, not only the Home page, so the cross-page portfolio identity stays consistent.
Wire the category filter so the grid re-filters and the readout reflects the live count/label each time a tab is clicked; do not leave a stale readout that never updates.
Do not use viewport-width font scaling, hidden-only benchmark text, placeholder images, remote stock media, or overflow-x:hidden hacks that leave the underlying fixed-width tab row overflowing.
state_constraints: desktop_home_initial, tablet_home_initial, and mobile_home_initial verify the portfolio loads across breakpoints with no horizontal overflow after the repair.

mobile_portfolio_grid verifies the repaired filter tab row fits a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow; the original-with-defect leg overflows about 294px and the broken restyle overflows about 314px.

desktop_portfolio_grid and mobile_portfolio_grid verify the project grid keeps Snapfolio's light visual language (white cards, readable titles, two-column rhythm) and reads as a coherent project grid, not a collapsed dark slab of overlapping cards.
desktop_portfolio_react verifies the category filter re-filters the grid and its readout advances after the React tab is clicked (interaction continuity).

desktop_about_rail, desktop_portfolio_rail, and mobile_about_rail verify the shared 'Selected work' rail is present on the About and Portfolio pages, not only the Home page (cross-page design continuity).
desktop_portfolio_initial verifies the Portfolio page and its six project cards remain visible; desktop_about_initial verifies the About page renders after the repair.

change_completion: The Portfolio page shows the project filter with all four category tabs, the live readout, the six project cards, and the shared 'Selected work' rail.
Clicking a category re-filters the grid and advances the readout, and the 'Selected work' rail is present on the About and Portfolio pages as well as the Home page.
design_consistency: The project grid and rail read as a coherent light Snapfolio design using soft emerald/rose gradients, white rounded cards, restrained slate typography, and a legible two-column grid.
The grid is not restyled into a dark collapsed slab, overlapping cards, or dark-on-dark text.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile states have no horizontal overflow, clipped nav, overlapped cards, or unstable tab widths.
Mobile keeps the filter tabs and project grid readable in a wrapped single-column rhythm with tappable controls.
regression: Original content signals Dimitriy Kuznet, Web Developer, the four filter categories, and the six project names remain visible.
Bundled assets src/images/portfolio_1.png and src/images/portfolio_2.png remain browser-visible and no remote media or new dependencies are introduced.

scoring_notes: A correct patch is a scoped design-continuity repair of the real Snapfolio portfolio: it makes the project filter's category tab row wrap so the 390px mobile Portfolio page has no horizontal overflow, keeps the project grid a clean legible light two-column grid, keeps the shared 'Selected work' rail present on every page (Home plus About and Portfolio), and keeps the category filter re-filtering the grid with a readout that tracks the tabs, while preserving the original portfolio content, the six project cards, the site navigation, the local images, and the desktop/tablet layouts. Leaving the fixed-width non-wrapping tab row (baseline) or a broken restyle that collapses the grid into a dark overlapping slab, drops the cross-page rail, and freezes the readout (bad) fails multiple gates: no_horizontal_overflow, visual_regression, dom_assertions (cross-page rail), and interaction_assertions (stale readout).
author_notes: Slot 318 targets feroz39/snapfolio for portfolio / Design Continuity / repair / cross_page, hardened to true-new-L4 on the repo's OWN native project browser. Snapfolio is a real multi-page Tailwind portfolio served as a static site; its Portfolio page already ships a category filter over a grid of six project cards, so the lever IS that native project-grid filter (no bolted-on metric strip). Four orthogonal levers realized through the filter: (D6) a fixed-width non-wrapping category tab row causes mobile horizontal overflow; (D3) the bad leg collapses the project grid into a dark slab whose cards shingle and overlap via negative margins with dark-on-dark titles; (D2) the shared 'Selected work' rail is dropped from the About and Portfolio pages; (D4) the filter readout is frozen by a stale closure so the click highlights the tab but the grid never filters. The reference repair fixes all four; the baseline fails D6/D3/D2 but passes D4 (its filter JS is correct); the bad leg fails all four. Content and DOM are identical across all legs; only the graded stylesheet pf-filter.css, the wiring script pf-filter.js, and the per-leg rail presence differ. The images portfolio_1.png and portfolio_2.png and the avatar.jpg asset stay browser-visible.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: A real multi-page developer-portfolio template that serves as a static site with shared navigation and a Portfolio page that natively hosts a category filter over a project-card grid, making it a natural L4 portfolio design-continuity repair with cross-page, visual, interaction, and responsive levers realized through the repo's own project browser.
